properties.name: Chattahoochee Brick Co.
properties.basis: OpenStreetMap via Nominatim: the centre of the site stated in the National Park Service's Historic American Landscapes Survey report, Chattahoochee Brick Company, HALS No. GA-7 ('33.809103, -84.490475 (Center of the Chattahoochee Brick Company site, Google Maps, WGS84)'); the report is in sources/ in this repository
properties.note: An 80-acre site; the point is its centre. The report places the 1907 building and railroad layout (from the 1907 Sanborn map) west of the centre and the 1907 convict-lease residences about 20 m from it; see the backdrop 'hals-ga-7-brick-site-plan' for the plan. The estimate made earlier from a Google Maps view (33.8093, -84.4895) was 90 m from this. The site is bounded by the Chattahoochee River (north), the CSX line (east), I-285 and Proctor Creek (west) and Parrott Avenue NW (south), and the entrance is at Brick Plant Road and Parrott Avenue. All the original buildings burned on December 2, 1900 and were rebuilt within a year; the plan shows the post-fire layout of 1907.
properties.date_source: Not dated: shown for the chapters and years canon/places.yml lists it under
